Subject: OpCo dedicated capacity intake & sizing - next meeting

Hi Claire —

Great to speak this morning. Quick recap of what we heard on the discovery call and a proposed next step so we can size dedicated capacity for your use case:

- Primary workload: multi-tenant customer support assistant + nightly batch embeddings for search indexing.
- Peak concurrent inference: ~180 concurrent requests during business hours (approx 09:00-18:00 ET).
- Typical request shape: short chat-turns (~50 tokens) and occasional long summarization jobs (~2k tokens).
- Current pain: latency spikes during peak and unpredictable unit costs.

Next step: schedule a dedicated sizing session (30–45m) with our Solutions Engineer to review sample traffic, confirm latency SLOs, and map to GPU pool sizing. For that call we'll want: one technical PM/engineer from your side, and your procurement contact if you want to cover any contract-level questions.

Proposed windows (PT):
- Tue 2026-09-21 10:00–10:45 PT
- Wed 2026-09-22 13:00–13:45 PT
- Thu 2026-09-23 08:30–09:15 PT

I attached a short capacity worksheet (redwood_capacity_template.xlsx) — if you can drop a sample export (CSV/JSON) of typical request rates + sequence length distribution ahead of the call, that will let us bring a preliminary sizing recommendation.

I’m cc’ing Priyom (AE) who will keep the deal and timeline on track. If any of those slots work, I’ll lock in the calendar and add Mina (SE) to the invite.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the summary and for the template. Tue 9/21 10:00 PT works for us — I'll block that now. I'll ask Jordan (Engineering lead) to join for the technical bits and loop in procurement in case we start talking terms.

A couple of clarifications from our discovery notes so the SE can prep:
- The 180 concurrent is our peak for customer-facing chat across our EU+US regions combined; APAC is currently small but expected to grow.
- Latency SLO: <= 220ms p95 for short chat turns; for long summarization jobs we expect throughput more than sub-200ms (we can accept higher latency for those if batching helps cost).
- We use sequence lengths up to ~2,500 tokens for nightly jobs (summarization + context enrichment).

We'll upload a 2-day sample of live traffic (anonymized) as opco_workload_sample.json into the Drive link you provided before the meeting.

See you Tue — I sent a calendar invite to Marcus, Jordan, and me.

Best,
Claire

Perfect — thanks Claire. I've tentatively accepted the invite for Tue 2026-09-21 10:00 PT and added Mina (our SE) and Priyom.

Quick prep notes for your team and Mina:
- If you can, include per-minute or per-second request timestamps and request token counts in the sample. Sequence length histogram is especially useful.
- Confirm whether you prefer strict p95 latency SLOs vs. cost-driven trade-offs (we commonly map three profiles: latency-first, balanced, cost-first).
- If there are any model constraints (specific model family, open-vs-licensed, or private weights), flag them ahead of time.

Agenda (30–45m):
1) 5m intro + goals
2) 15–20m workload review & sizing assumptions
3) 10m preliminary GPU pool sizing and cost/latency trade-offs
4) 5–10m next steps + procurement sync

I also uploaded a short draft SLA we typically use for Dedicated customers (SLA-draft.pdf) — procurement can look ahead of the call.

If anything changes, ping me here; otherwise we’ll come prepared with two sizing options (low-latency and cost-optimized).

Thanks,
Marcus

Subject: Re: OpCo dedicated capacity intake & sizing - technical checklist

Hi all —

Thanks for the invite — I’ll lead the sizing portion. A couple of technical checklist items so we can hit the ground running on Tue: 

- Sample payloads (anonymized) for short chat and summarization jobs (JSON ok).
- Expected concurrency distribution by hour (simple table or CSV).
- Typical max sequence length (you mentioned ~2,500; can you confirm 2,500 max or are there outliers?).
- Desired p50/p95/p99 latency targets and any SLAs that matter for failover/regional redundancy.
- Are embeddings run inline or as a separate batch pipeline? If inline, include the per-request embed calls.

If you can drop the opco_workload_sample.json into the Drive folder and add a short README (1–2 bullets) describing fields, that will let me pre-run a quick sizing script and have two recommended configs ready.

Also, do you have an internal contact for network/egress constraints? For dedicated deployments we usually validate region-level egress/firewall expectations.

See you Tue.

— Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
